task: Source-only initial subscription/hydration/read-proof diagnosis for original first-pair SQL RED
head: 1ffa581f16319381054e0636ae41e6292719a1fe

facts: useLiveKeys uses Provider.workspaceId only when its workspaceId argument is undefined; explicit null is retained.
Effect lifetime includes the effective scope, serialized entities/keys, cache, mutate, share, owner and namespace.
LiveProvider retains one LiveChannels object per owner; changing its workspaceId prop alone does not allocate a new object or open a connection.
LiveChannels creates a channel only upon an actual subscription and removes it when its final subscriber leaves.
ownerListWorkspace returns null until a matching-owner response supplies a valid owned-home UUID.
Task runs, chat summaries and thread list explicitly pass that home, including null.
Issue list and roster explicitly pass their selected/read scope; workspace_settings explicitly passes workspaceHome and owns workspace/switcher, workspace, teams and project-teams invalidations.
DesktopIntegration uses the same explicit-home task-run hook; it is not an independent default-scope connection anchor.
Consequently, setting only the Provider bootstrap workspace does not establish an earlier channel for these actual callers.
Both web and Native ticket functions return null for an unresolved scope.
A newly opened socket invalidates to cover its connection gap; readiness captures a new same-realm ordering boundary.
readFresh requires a later actual read, a committed current cache object, no supersession/error, and all required/held revisions.
The observer may promote its start boundary using an actual response object's dispatch WeakMap proof; it does not treat arbitrary stored data as freshness.
Before-ready reads, reconnects, new actual scopes and permission failures retain the ordinary catch-up requirement.
PersistentReadCache.hydrate has a started guard and resolves one hydration promise; its restoration does not count as fresh network data.
HydrateReadCache resumes only while its effect remains mounted and depends on cache/mutate.

staleOnFocus pauses before SWR starts while hydration is incomplete, then registers one bound revalidator per mounted key; resumeHydrationReads chooses one reader for each key and skips freshly committed data.
The Native AuthenticatedReadCache creates a stable cache per authorized namespace; IssueWorkspace withinLiveProvider does not add another cache boundary.
ViewStateProvider changes its context store on scope change but has no keyed children or SWR provider remount.
No concrete duplicate hydration/resume path has been established in the inspected actual mount path.
The first Native readBatch includes task-runs.pollTaskRuns, chat summaries and bot roster under the same HTTP request.
Task runs occurs once while chat summaries and roster occur twice, so a blanket claim that every Native batch lost dispatch proof is unsupported.
Original server receipts do not include JavaScript readBoundary values, effective live-scope transitions or client open/ready observations.
Server timestamps/count differences alone do not distinguish a legitimate first watch-gap read from lost proof or a needless subscription restart.

cases: committed post-ready read covers pending flush
late subscription on continuously ready connection reuses committed read
before/no readiness, new push and earlier generation still read
discarded/replaced cache value and failed read do not certify freshness
retired owner cannot start or adopt another read
resolving owned home preserves selected channel; unresolved home never guesses Provider scope
actual Native queue/codec/MessageChannel snapshot proofs for task runs, summaries and roster: before readiness reads twice, after readiness once
real React/SWR hydration and StrictMode expect exactly one fresh read
empty/failed disk starts a cold read
server seed and optimistic value outrank disk
document departure preserves retired boundary and cleanup

regressionProposal.runtime: Existing real React, SWR, LiveChannels, staleOnFocus, Native callAction/read-batch/codec and runtime MessageChannel; add actual PersistentReadCache and HydrateReadCache with fixture-only storage and authenticated HTTP/WS boundaries.
requiredEventOrder: cache activation and each restored scoped key
actual accepted cache object and revision
live flush and any trailing request

cases.name: provider-hint-negative-control
cases.purpose: Use actual list hooks with explicit unresolved home and compare Provider workspace undefined versus authorized hint. Neither may guess an owner-home ticket or skip the first required catch-up. Do not manufacture a default-scope anchor absent from production.

cases.name: same-scope-covered-dispatch
cases.purpose: With a legitimate existing scoped subscription and a real hydrated snapshot, control capability acknowledgement before actual Native HTTP dispatch. Once the exact result commits with sufficient revisions, an additional identical read must not occur. A failure here would be a meaningful RED requiring trace-local explanation.

cases.name: uncovered-or-new-generation
cases.purpose: Move acknowledgement after actual dispatch, reconnect, or change actual workspace/owner. Require the later fresh read and prove late old results cannot populate or refresh the new scope.

cases.name: hydration-and-revision-boundaries
cases.purpose: Preserve fresh initial network validation, empty/failed storage, StrictMode, fresh-vs-disk precedence, discarded/comparator-retained data, higher required revision, permission failures and retired cache.

regressionProposal.redGreenRule: Do not claim RED/GREEN until the actual baseline fixture runs. If the covered-dispatch test already passes, reject that candidate rather than relaxing its guards or counting mandatory gap reads as duplicates.
bootstrapGuardIfFurtherProposed: fresh bootstrap owner must match current user
requested selector must be compatible with the authorized bootstrap scope
fresh matching read supersedes a bootstrap hint
mismatched owner, denial/error and changed selector cannot fall back to former authorization
null owned-home from owner-wide list remains null; selected workspace is not a substitute for owned home

minimumChangeAssessment.providerHintAlone: Not demonstrated to affect the targeted actual consumers; do not publish it as a 44-query fix.
minimumChangeAssessment.genericHydrationOrReadFresh: No justified source change identified; retain initial authoritative read and all existing revision/lifetime guards.

Root owns Native dispatch whitelist review; these could be reviewed as separate exact-result proof candidates, with actual before/after readiness tests. They do not by themselves establish resolution of the 44-query deficit.
